sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the Judgment and award dated 28.06.2022 passed in MVC No.558/2022 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM and Addl. MACT, Bidar (for short 'the tribunal') seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. The claimant aged 42 years working as agricultural labour met with accident on 15.02.2018 and sustained grievous injuries.
She filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.7,55,000/- along with interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

The tribunal after considering the NC: 2025:KHC-K:7427 HC-KAR entire evidence on record, awarded a sum of Rs.1,32,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Being aggrieved by the said Judgment and award the claimant preferred the present appeal and mainly contended that at the time of the accident the claimant was aged 39 years and he was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.
The tribunal not considering the said aspect, has awarded meager amounts.
She sustained three injuries, out of which one is grievous in nature.
Further it is stated that, no amounts are granted for loss of future earning capacity and loss of amenities and thus requested for enhancement of the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the claimant has stated that, the claimant has not been examined by the Doctor.

He relied on the Judgment dated 17.06.2016 of this Court passed in MFA No.1556/2016 [Ramachandra S/o. Munipapaiah Vs. Girija K and another], and argued that, the claimant has suffered multiple fracture to her head and fracture of distal end of right clavicle and fracture of right Shantamma W/O Pundlik vs Mahatab Mahatab S/O Ahmedsab Qureshi on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62073345/
2 zygomatic bone.

sentences.text: As per the wound certificate she sustained one fracture NC: 2025:KHC-K:7427 HC-KAR and two simple injuries.
The claimant was hospitalized for four days.
The claimant has not filed any income proof.
She met with accident in the year 2018.
Therefore, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, her income is to be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance company contends that, the claimant herself has stated in her claim petition that, she was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month, the same has to be taken into consideration for calculation of the compensation.
5. Heard the arguments from both sides.
6.
It is a beneficial legislation.
The Courts are relying upon the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for assessment of the income of the claimants and deceased, where there is no income proof.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to consider the income of the claimant at Rs.11,750/- per month.
As per Ex.P.4 - wound certificate she was aged 42 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, the multiplier is 14.
In this case as NC: 2025:KHC-K:7427 HC-KAR there is no disability certificate, question of granting future earning capacity does not arise.

Considering the nature of injuries, period of hospitalization, age of the claimant and her occupation,
this Court finds it reasonable to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering,
Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The claimant might have not attended any other work for at least three months.
Hence, she is entitled for a sum of Rs.35,250/- (Rs.11,750/- X 3 months), under the head loss of earning during laid up period.
As per Ex.P.8 the claimant has filed medical bills to an extent of Rs.66,730/-.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to award a sum of Rs.66,730/- towards medical bills.

Hence, the total compensation is as under:
